description.value: The study validated a modified Empathic Accuracy Task using naturalistic autobiographical emotional videos, continuous ratings of perceived emotional intensity, and a neutral control condition, while examining neural correlates of emotional processing, empathic accuracy, and affect sharing.

design.value: A staged fMRI study in which healthy participants watched six autobiographical video clips, comprising two sad, two happy and two neutral clips, while continuously rating the narrator's emotional intensity. The study also included a separate normative, non-imaging EAT sample and a pilot sample used to select the fMRI clips.

description.value: Participants in a pilot study used to select the six fMRI video clips.

task_description.value: Participants watched and rated six video clips in a fixed order: one happy, one sad and one neutral video featuring one female and one male target. They continuously rated the perceived emotional intensity of the target while watching each clip.

instructions.value: Participants were instructed to continuously rate the perceived emotional intensity of the target using the same 9-point scale, from 1, 'no emotion' to 9, 'very strong emotion'. Following each clip, they reported which emotion the target felt most strongly and which emotion they themselves felt most strongly.

stimuli.value: Autobiographical emotional video clips of people talking about an event: happy, sad and neutral clips. Neutral targets described their bedroom.

description.value: EPI files were reoriented, slice-time corrected, realigned, coregistered to the T1-weighted image, normalised to MNI space using group-wise DARTEL registration, resampled to 1.5 mm isotropic voxels, spatially smoothed with an 8 mm Gaussian FWHM kernel, and followed by extraction of a CSF time-course signal.

model_settings.value: Block design with three regressors, happy, sad and neutral, formed by convolution of the canonical HRF with boxcars delimiting video presentation. Separate parameter estimates were produced for emotional and neutral categories compared to the implicit baseline.
Paired t-tests identified clusters differentially activated for emotional versus neutral video clips and for happy versus sad clips.

model_type.value: general linear model with parametric modulation

model_settings.value: Z-EA scores for each participant and each video clip were added as parametric modulators at the first level.
One-sample t-tests tested whether the BOLD response during emotional video clips was modulated by intra-individual variations in Z-EA scores.
Scans were split and a model was fitted to each emotional video clip in turn. Continuous ratings of the target's emotional intensity for each 2 s bin were entered as regressors of interest.
One-sample t-tests assessed whether the relationship between BOLD response and changes in emotional intensity ratings was observed across the group.

A block design with three separate conditions, shared, non-shared and neutral, was created for the 20 participants who showed affect sharing in response to some but not all video clips. Separate parameter estimates were calculated for each condition compared to the implicit baseline.
Paired t-tests identified clusters differentially activated when watching video clips that induced affect sharing compared to non-shared clips.

Paired t-tests examined differences in Z-transformed EA scores, affective and cognitive empathy scores, target emotional-intensity ratings, and Z-EA scores for affect-sharing versus non-sharing clips. Pearson correlations tested relationships between mean Z-EA scores, IRI subscales and IQ, and relationships between normative and scanner-based Z-EA scores.
